title: The Concept of Social Structure in Functionalism
text:
Functionalist theory views society as a complex system whose various parts work together to promote the overall stability and existence of the whole. From this perspective, social structures—such as the family, education system, and economy—are seen as performing specific functions that contribute to societal equilibrium.

Dysfunction is understood not merely as failure, but as any element that disrupts the integrated functioning of a major social mechanism. Theorists argue that every institution maintains a vital role in upholding shared norms and values, which collectively provide coherence to the culture.
